Hi Alice — thanks, and great questions. I put together a short summary and attached the pricing table and a redlineable burst addendum for legal. Key points below and a worked example at the end.

1) Burst headroom (how many extra GPUs)
- Default overlay: 50% of committed pool per region (e.g., commit 8 GPUs -> baseline pool = 8; default burst headroom = up to 4 additional GPUs).
- Enterprise add-on: we can enable "expanded overlay" up to 100% of commit for qualified customers (requires a 6-month notice period and a soft capacity reservation).
- Headroom is provisioned regionally and is governed by available capacity and your committed commit class (we prioritize committed pools when capacity is constrained).

2) Billing & multipliers
- Billing unit: per-minute metering with billing pro-rated to the minute. We report per-hour aggregated costs on invoices.
- Pricing model: committed GPUs billed at committed rate (example below). Burst overlay uses a tiered multiplier: 1.8x the committed rate for the first 4 vGPU-hours per day, then 1.25x for additional burst usage that day. This rewards short, elastic bursts but keeps extended burst economics reasonable.

3) Cooldown rules and exceptions
- Cooldown trigger: a sustained burst >25% above commit for longer than 10 consecutive minutes triggers the cooldown.
- Cooldown window: default rolling cooldown of 30 minutes where additional bursts are evaluated against the multiplier tiers.
- Scheduled events: we offer a Scheduled Event Waiver — submit a 48-hour advance notice and we can carve out a one-time exemption (or negotiate an Event Window in the SOW for recurring launches). For >24h planned events we recommend a temporary, short-term commit bump to avoid overlay charges.

4) Throughput guarantees and SLA
- Base SLO: committed pool backed by a throughput SLO (p99 latency target and a per-minute throughput baseline). Burst overlay is not generally SLA-backed unless covered by a separate Peak Throughput SLA addendum (we can include for enterprise with a 20% surcharge on committed rate and a minimum 3-month duration).

Worked example (net-of-discounts):
- Commit: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) at committed rate = $12.00/GPU-hour (after commit discount).
- Default headroom: +4 GPUs allowed as burst overlay.
- Burst billing: first 4 vGPU-hours/day @1.8x = $21.60/GPU-hour; additional burst hours that day @1.25x = $15.00/GPU-hour.
- If you hit a sustained burst that triggers cooldown, subsequent bursts within the 30-min cooldown are billed with the same tiering but we monitor to avoid oscillation.

Looping in Marissa on pricing mechanics. A couple of internal notes / asks before we finalize the redline: 

- For strategic accounts like AMX we should propose a slightly flatter burst multiplier structure — propose 1.6x for first 6 vGPU-hours/day and 1.15x afterwards. This helps win vs cloud alternatives where customers fear 3x+ surges.
- Offer a "term hold": allow them to lock an expanded overlay for 14 days on signature while we finalize a short-term commit. That reduces procurement friction.
- Legal will want the Scheduled Event Waiver to require explicit start/end times and a one-email approval chain to make it auditable.
